Let's be honest, nobody plays Just Cause 3 for the story... and that's completely fine.

The story is forgettable, but that's not what this game is trying to sell. The real reason to play is the insane freedom it gives you. You can fly across the map with your wingsuit, grapple onto almost anything, blow up entire military bases, steal whatever vehicle you want, and create your own ridiculous moments.

The map is beautiful, colorful, and surprisingly fun to explore. Sometimes I completely forgot about the missions and just spent hours causing as much chaos as possible.

The gameplay is pure sandbox fun, and very few games let you mess around on this level.

My only complaint is that once you've seen most of what the game has to offer, it doesn't have a lot of replay value. It's an amazing ride the first time, but I didn't really feel like coming back after finishing it.

If you're looking for a serious story, this isn't it. If you just want to relax, blow everything up, and have fun for hours, Just Cause 3 absolutely delivers.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the movement mechanics, praising the combination of the grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit for traversal.

citations.review_text:
This is one of those times I wish Steam had a Neutral option for reviews since, although there's a lot to fun to be had in this game.....there's also a lot of stuff that's annoying or repetitive to deal with as well.

The Good:

- The grappling hook/wingsuit combo is absolutely a joy to use to get around and makes using any other method of getting around pointless (more on that in a bit). Swooping in and then floating 100 feet above a base as you rain destruction down is what this game does best.

- It looks pretty nice and the explosions are satisfying.

- Using the grappling hook as a weapon works well when you have the opportunity to do it instead of desperately running from enemies (see below). I know they built on it in the next game.

- Most of the side activities are pretty fun to do.

- There is a bit of strategy involved in taking out bigger installations. Hacking anti-air to take out helicopters (or let you fly in with one more freely), deciding how to destroy something with either the grapple or a weapon or other means. There probably could have been more of that, honestly.

The Bad:

- The upgrade system is full of pointless upgrades and I'm not a fan of tying them to the side activities. The ones that upgrade the grapple are spread out so much that its annoying. Just go full Saints Row 3 with the power fantasy and let me upgrade so I have a Rico immune to bullets with infinite RPG ammo by the end of the game.

- What's the point of the Chaos score now? In JC 2 you unlocked the next story mission after hitting a certain score and unlocked more weapons and vehicles. What does it do in this game? Why couldn't it be tied to the upgrade system in this game too?

- Vehicles are pointless AND they handle like crap, especially bigger vehicles.

- A LOT of the areas and bases look the same and you are blowing up the same stuff over and over. Stop making me follow pipes Dimah! The story missions are also way less fun than just flying around …

i think its a slight upgrade to the jc2, the characters are funny but dont try too much(it feels natural and not forced), tom sheldon is not american enough though, and i wish the the va for rico from jc2 was in this game... but they more than make up for it, it runs good, looks good, expecting the driving to be mid compared to the last game, but i waas wrong (except for the bikes), they added rudder control witch made combat aircraft actually viable in combat and mutch easier to fly, they added  the wingsuit(awesome) wish the grappling  hook and parachute combo was a bit more like in jc2 (i mean its slowed down, but then it wouldnt make the wingsuit that mutch viable now would it?) the tether-tether is straight up better, you can use technically an infinite amount of explosives to destroy things, but you got to get close to use  them wich i think is good balancing. the world progression feels a bit more aware(in the sense that they atcually explain how destroying bases affects the ennemy instead of just telling you to destroy ♥♥♥♥ like in jc2 ,over all i think its a really fun game and you should try it

Just Cause 3 nails the open-world sandbox formula. The combo mechanics of the Grappling Hook, Parachute, and Wingsuit make movement feel incredibly fluid and addictive. The map is massive, beautiful, and practically begs you to destroy it. If you want a game where you can cause creative chaos without any limits, this is a must-have in your library.

citations.review_text: Very fun, great movement and environment, my only problem with the game is that 2 of the achievements, Caught em all and Supply and demand simply refuse to register. Ive completed the entire game twice now, and yet the achievements fail to be assigned to my steam account. Other than that, great game.

Gameplay is greatly improved from Just Cause 2 but some components such as "challenges" felt more like chores. These are optional but some features of your equipment, one example being precision aim (kinda like ADS), are locked behind completing a certain amount of these. 

Liberating settlements themselves feel great though, especially since the graphics are vastly improved from its predecessor. The towns look beautiful and the cities look way better now. That being said, there aren't many landmarks really or memorable locations and everything at some point will look the same. The scenery and variety isn't all that great compared to JC2.

Combat is good, and there are a plethora of weapons. Driving isn't as bad as I though it would be. Some cars actually handle pretty well. The motorcycle handling is terrible though. Flying helicopters and planes are great, though you'll probably benefit from changing key bindings. I couldn't do some changes directly in game for some reason, but you can edit the file for the bindings. Boats also handle fine.

Just Cause 3 added a wingsuit and later on if you have the dlc, a bavarium wingsuit (basically  a wingsuit but with thrusters), which make traversal really enjoyable. There are no save files which is a bummer, but you can reset settlements to free them again.

There are some bugs I encountered when doing some challenges and one related to an achievement. Also somehow I didn't care about the story and the characters in it probably because it wanted to be goofy and serious at the same time which didn't really resonate with me. The story isn't really the point of the series though but it would have been better to have something compelling or something to engage you especially since gameplay can become repetitive real quick.

When this game goes on sale, it can go down to a very low price and that's when I suggest you buy XXL edition of the game.

[h2] A timeless sandbox game that never gets old [/h2]


[b]The Good:[/b]

Incredibly fun traversal features like the wingsuit and grappling hook.
Massive open world with collectibles spread all over.
Destruction that never stops being satisfying.
Beautiful Mediterranean-inspired setting.
Tons of freedom to approach objectives however the player chooses.

[b]The Bad:[/b]

Story is bland.
Repetitive side activities (Trying to get that perfect score).
Physics occasionally decide to become comedy instead of realism (Ramming into cars while in another car makes them fling up in the air & exploding).


[h2]Entertaining Gameplay[/h2]

Just Cause 3 is absolute chaos in the best way. You're not here for a deep narrative, you are however, here to liberate islands by destroying Medici Military bases. As well as destroying gas containers or electric boxes in towns/cities to liberate them. Some places on the map are fairly easy to liberate, while heavily guarded ones with many enemies in them.

The grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit create one of the most enjoyable movement systems I've experienced in an open-world game. Traversing the map is so much fun that fast travel almost feels unnecessary. Gliding across the terrain with the wingsuit and grappling hook offers the player many beautiful sunsets or stary nights.

[h2]The Graphics & Atmosphere[/h2]

The world is colorful, vibrant, and packed with gorgeous views. Flying across mountains before diving into a military base never gets old. Even years after release, the game still looks great. As I said previously, it makes the fast travel feature feel unnecessary.

[h2]Overall Thoughts[/h2]

If you enjoy sandbox games that prioritize fun over realism, this is an easy recommendation. It embraces over-the-top action packed scenes and gives you endless ways to create your own ridiculous, and possibly funny moments.

Just Cause 3 can be described in a single word: Awesome! 

There is tons of destruction and explosions. The combat feels engaging and the dialogue is humorous. The story is alright, but nothing phenomenal. The open world is massive and looks pretty nice. The destruction physics are a great source of fun. 

The DLCs offer great extra content. More things to destroy and things to collect, in addition to new and exciting weapons. 

Shooting from a driving train, hacking SAM turrets, parachuting, wingsuiting, flying a jet or blasting everyone in a tank. This game is awesome.

There are some rare instances where the physics glitch out and you either get stuck in the ground or shoot into the sky. 

Some of the challenges are actually bugged and therefore impossible, so 100%'ing the game will likely not happen. At least not without creative workarounds. 

From a technical perspective, I experience very few game breaking problems. The game never crashed or froze for me. It runs pretty smooth and the graphics are gorgeous. 

Final verdict: awesome game. Definitely recommend it!

[h2]Entertaining Gameplay[/h2]

As well as destroying gas containers or electric boxes in towns/cities to liberate them. Some places on the map are fairly easy to liberate, while heavily guarded ones with many enemies in them.

The grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit create one of the most enjoyable movement systems I've experienced in an open-world game. The world is colorful, vibrant, and packed with gorgeous views. Flying across mountains before diving into a military base never gets old. Even years after release, the game still looks great. As I said previously, it makes the fast travel feature feel unnecessary.

[h2]Overall Thoughts[/h2]

If you enjoy sandbox games that prioritize fun over realism, this is an easy recommendation. It embraces over-the-top action packed scenes and gives you endless ways to create your own ridiculous, and possibly funny moments.

*Just Cause 3* is the kind of game that does not need a deep story to be fun. It knows exactly what kind of chaos it wants to give you, and when it works, it is incredibly entertaining.

The story is very simple. Rico Rodriguez returns to Medici, his homeland, to help overthrow General Di Ravello, a dictator who controls the islands through fear, military power and Bavarium. To be honest, the plot is not the reason I like this game. Di Ravello is not a very complex villain, and the rebellion story is pretty straightforward. But somehow, that fits the game. Rico is not here for quiet drama. He is here to turn an entire military regime into fireworks.

Medici is a big reason why the game feels good. The islands are sunny, colorful and beautiful, with mountains, villages, military bases, beaches and blue water everywhere. It is almost funny how pretty the world looks while you are blowing half of it up. One moment you are gliding peacefully over the sea with the wingsuit, and the next moment you are crashing into a fuel tank, pulling down a statue, or sending enemy vehicles flying off a cliff.

The movement is easily the best part. The grappling hook, parachute and wingsuit make Rico feel like a superhero with no respect for physics. Just moving across the map is fun. I can spend a long time doing nothing important, just launching myself into the air, gliding between mountains, grappling onto cars, jumping onto helicopters and finding stupid ways to travel. A lot of open-world games make travel feel like empty distance, but in *Just Cause 3*, movement itself is the game.

The destruction is also extremely satisfying. Liberating towns and bases can get repetitive, but the act of doing it rarely stops being fun.
